Remaining leads: www.bamsoftware.com/git/dnstt.git/dns (unresolved_control_failure), github.com/cybergarage/go-mdns/mdns/dns (unresolved_control_failure), github.com/soypat/seqs/eth/dns (unresolved_control_failure), github.com/nadoo/glider/dns (unresolved_control_failure). Rounds 1-3 used pkg.go.dev package searches (dns, dns message, dns parser, dns packet; then dns wire, dns codec, dns decode, dns unpack, dnsmessage, mdns, dns rr); round 4 used GitHub repository searches, awesome lists, reverse dependencies and forks of the selected decoders, and binary-format decoder tools (registry-snapshot.json round4_discovery). Round 5 (2026-11-18) used new pkg.go.dev routes (round5_discovery): symbol searches for DNS message types and decoders (dns.Msg, dns.Message, dns.Unpack, dns.Parse, dns.ParseMessage, dns.Decode, dns.UnmarshalMessage, dns.Packet, dns.Header, dns.Question, dns.RR, dns.ResourceRecord, ParseDNS, DecodeDNS, UnpackDNS, DNSMessage, DNSPacket, ParseDNSPacket, DecodeDNSMessage, ParseDNSMessage, mdns.Message, dnsmsg.Message, dnsmessage.Message) and package searches (RFC 1035, rfc1035, dns message decode, dns wire format, dns protocol, dns packet parser, domain name system), first 100 each, ranked only by the same imported-by count (round5_targeted). It found github.com/shadowy-pycoder/mshark/layers (selected: the DNS layer of a packet analyser, its own decoder). Round-5 exclusions: shuLhan/share lib/dns (own decoder but no exported way to pass message bytes), soypat/seqs eth/dns and nadoo/glider dns (RDATA kept raw, the dnstt precedent), tachyon udwDnsPacket (drops classes and merges sections), gonq (header only), v2ray protocol/dns and coroot's l7 (x/net dnsmessage), likexian/doh (JSON types), winstonprivacyinc/dns (benburkert/dns copy) and five miekg/dns snapshots or clones (Psiphon-Labs/Psiphon-Inc, tonnerre, cloudflare, AZ-X; 81-100% of their lines in a miekg/dns revision); the other symbol hits were vendored miekg/dns copies, DNS-provider APIs or zone tools recognised by path and not opened. gopacket's and mshark's counts cover their whole multi-protocol layers packages. The standard library exports no DNS message parser (its net resolver vendors x/net dnsmessage without exporting it). Each verified path parses the two valid controls (a query and a response with compressed CNAME/A/AAAA/MX answers) to the hand-written oracle summary, has library source coverage and stable AFL++ feedback that differs between the controls. Two valid controls do not establish EDNS0, DNSSEC, TXT, authority/additional or malformed-input behaviour. Package-level adoption metrics include non-DNS use, and the cell is not a definitive top ten.
